How to use it

  1. Upload the entity export. The MID column is what makes this work.
  2. Read the high-severity clusters first — those share an identifier.
  3. Decide, per cluster, whether the variants are one thing or several.
  4. Choose one canonical form and record it.
  5. Leave case-only differences switched off unless you have a specific reason.

Worth knowing. Not every cluster is an error. “Google” and “Google Cloud” are different things; “LLM” and “LLMs” are not.

Your entity export

Upload the entity_mentions.csv from the Entity Extractor. The mid column is what makes this work: entities sharing a Knowledge Graph MID are the same thing by definition.
Needs an entity column. Types and MIDs unlock more checks.
Case-only differences (content / Content / CONTENT) are excluded by default. In the MLforSEO corpus they were 94% of all clusters and none of it was actionable. Turn them on only if you have a specific reason.
